purpose: Clindamycin palmitate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the skin, lungs, throat, and other parts of the body. It is often used for children because it comes as a flavored liquid that is easier to swallow. It only works against bacterial infections and will not help with colds, flu, or viral illnesses.
how_it_works: This medicine works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply. Think of it like cutting off the bacteria's food supply — without those proteins, the bacteria can't survive or spread. Over time, your immune system can then clear the remaining bacteria from your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, stomach pain, and vomiting. Some people may notice a skin rash. The liquid form may cause a temporary unpleasant taste in your mouth.
warnings: A very important warning: if you develop severe or bloody diarrhea during or even weeks after finishing this medication, contact your doctor right away, as this could be a serious gut infection called C. difficile. Tell your doctor if you are allergic to clindamycin or lincomycin. Avoid taking it if you have a history of certain bowel diseases unless your doctor says it is safe. Always finish the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better.
typical_dosing: For children, the usual dose is based on body weight and is given by mouth every 6 to 8 hours (3 to 4 times a day). Your doctor or pharmacist will calculate the right dose for your child. Always use the measuring device provided — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Adults typically use a different form of clindamycin, but dosing is always determined by your healthcare provider.
